documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY -- Follow-up 01/09/2024

Ms. Strong returns after missing her September visit. Seen 6/2023 for cushingoid features; 1 mg overnight dexamethasone test 6/20/2023 did not suppress (8 AM cortisol 4.1 mcg/dL).

Interval: still bruising easily, face still round, weight up (also on olanzapine since May). Cycles irregular. No fractures. Mood steady with psychiatry.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly. NKDA.

Exam: BP 142/88. Rounded facies, dorsocervical fat pad, thin skin with forearm bruises, violaceous lower abdominal striae. Proximal strength normal.

Today: ACTH drawn; 24-hour urine free cortisol collection completed this morning.

Plan: MRI pituitary with and without contrast. We will call with results and see her in February to choose treatment.

Addendum 1/11: ACTH 46 pg/mL (ref 7.2-63) -- not suppressed, so this is ACTH-dependent. 24-hour urine free cortisol 162 mcg/24 h (ref 4-50), about three times the upper limit. MRI booked 1/30; patient informed.

Endocrinology

documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY -- 02/13/2024

Results reviewed with Ms. Strong:
- 1 mg dexamethasone test 6/2023: cortisol 4.1, not suppressed.
- 24-hour urine free cortisol 162 mcg/24 h (ref 4-50).
- ACTH 46 pg/mL, not suppressed: ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome.
- MRI pituitary 1/30: normal gland, no adenoma.
- Adrenal glands and pancreas normal on her MRI abdomen 2/2023 (VHL surveillance).

No source has been found that surgery could target, so we will control the cortisol medically.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Cushingoid features unchanged.
Baseline today: ALT 21 U/L. ECG: sinus rhythm, normal intervals, QTc 426 ms.

Plan:
- Start ketoconazole 200 mg by mouth twice daily with food. Avoid antacids and acid reducers around doses.
- It is not safe in pregnancy; she will avoid pregnancy while taking it.
- Signs of low cortisol reviewed (unusual tiredness, nausea, dizziness, poor appetite) -- call us if they occur.
- ALT and 24-hour urine free cortisol 4 weeks after starting and 4 weeks after any dose change, then at visits every 6 months. Goal urine free cortisol 50 or less. Stop for ALT above 168 (3 times the upper limit).

Endocrinology

EXAM: MRI abdomen without and with IV gadolinium, renal protocol.
INDICATION: VHL, surveillance of right renal lesion, solitary kidney.

FINDINGS: Right interpolar solid enhancing lesion now 2.2 x 2.0 cm (previously 2.0 x 1.9 cm). Simple right renal cysts unchanged, largest 1.4 cm. No new solid lesion. No hydronephrosis. Left nephrectomy bed clear. Adrenal glands normal. Pancreas normal. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Slight interval growth of the solid right renal lesion, now 2.2 cm. Stable simple cysts. Adrenals and pancreas unremarkable.

events.reason: Recurrent confusion and sweating relieved by eating

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department -- Physician Record
Visit: 05/27/2024, arrived 16:40

CC: episodes of confusion and sweating.

HPI: 35-year-old woman with Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, Cushing syndrome and type 2 diabetes presents with recurrent spells of confusion and diaphoresis, mostly in the late afternoon. Each resolves after she eats candy. Diabetes managed with metformin and diet. Denies insulin, sulfonylureas, any other prescription or over-the-counter medications, or herbal supplements.

PMH: VHL (cerebellar/spinal hemangioblastomas, retinal angiomas, right renal lesion), clear cell RCC s/p L nephrectomy, T2DM, HTN, Cushing syndrome, PCOS, bipolar I.
Meds: ketoconazole 200 mg tid, olanzapine 10 mg qhs, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (metformin per HPI).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father VHL; mother T2DM, HTN; maternal uncle bipolar.
SH: never smoker, 1-2 drinks monthly, part-time administrative assistant.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 78, afebrile. Well-appearing. BMI 29. Alert and oriented, no focal deficits. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen benign.

ED course: fingerstick glucose 45 on arrival during a spell; given juice and crackers with resolution. A second episode was observed in the department at 18:20: serum glucose 40. Critical-sample labs drawn at that time (insulin, C-peptide, sulfonylurea screen), then treated with oral glucose.

MDM: Recurrent hypoglycemia; her only glucose-lowering drug is metformin, which does not cause hypoglycemia. Concern for endogenous hyperinsulinism vs. surreptitious agent. Labs pending.

Disposition: placed in observation for glucose monitoring.

Emergency Medicine

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Observation Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
OBSERVATION DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 05/27/2024 (observation)   Discharge: 05/28/2024

Reason: recurrent hypoglycemia.

Course: Admitted from the ED to observation with fingerstick checks every 2 hours and frequent meals. No further hypoglycemia overnight. Critical-sample results from the ED episode: serum glucose 40 mg/dL, insulin 45 uIU/mL (ref 2-25), C-peptide 1.2 ng/mL (ref 1.1-4.4). Insulin and C-peptide inappropriately unsuppressed during hypoglycemia, consistent with endogenous hyperinsulinemia. Sulfonylurea screen sent out, pending at discharge.

Discharge diagnosis: hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (hyperinsulinemia).

Discharge medications: no changes -- metformin 1000 mg BID, olanzapine 10 mg qhs, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, ketoconazole 200 mg tid.
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: small frequent meals and a bedtime snack; carry glucose tablets; check fingerstick with any spell. Follow up with PCP within one week and with her endocrinologist for further evaluation.

Hospital Medicine

CC: headaches, dizziness, left eye.

Since about the spring her headaches are more frequent and she gets spells of dizziness. Over the last few weeks the left eye is blurry and she thinks part of the vision in that eye is missing. No falls, no weakness, no numbness, no vomiting. No hypoglycemia spells -- fingersticks normal during the dizzy episodes she has checked.

Exam: BP 156/88. Alert. Confrontation fields full OD; OS she describes part of the field as missing, hard to map in the office. Pupils equal and reactive. EOM full. Rest of CN intact. Strength and sensation normal. Finger-nose normal. Gait normal, tandem slightly cautious.

Headaches/dizziness with known cerebellar hemangioblastoma -- overdue for neurology follow-up and MRI. Neurology referral, asked for earliest available.
L eye vision change, h/o L retinal angiomas -- ophthalmology referral, urgent.
Return precautions: worst headache, vomiting, imbalance, weakness -- ED.

EXAM: MRI brain without and with IV gadolinium.
INDICATION: VHL, headaches and dizziness.
COMPARISON: MRI 12/14/2022.
FINDINGS: Left cerebellar hemisphere mass with nodular enhancement, now 1.4 cm (previously 1.1 cm), abutting the pial surface, without cyst or surrounding edema. Small inferior vermian enhancing nodule unchanged at 0.6 cm. Fourth ventricle normal; no hydrocephalus. No new lesion. Supratentorial brain normal.
reports.conclusion: Left cerebellar mass with nodular enhancement consistent with hemangioblastoma, 1.4 cm, mildly enlarged since 2022. Stable vermian lesion. No hydrocephalus.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology -- return visit 11/26/2024

Ms. Strong, known VHL, returns with six months of headaches and episodic dizziness and, more recently, blurring and partial loss of vision in the left eye.

PMH: VHL with cerebellar and spinal hemangioblastomas and left retinal angiomas, clear cell RCC s/p left radical nephrectomy, T2DM, HTN, Cushing syndrome, PCOS, bipolar I, hyperinsulinemia.
Meds: olanzapine 10 mg qhs, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, ketoconazole 200 mg tid. NKDA.
Family history: a cousin had a similar kidney tumor and an uncle died of complications from a brain tumor (in addition to her father's VHL and brother's brain tumor).
Social: never smoker, 1-2 drinks monthly, part-time administrative assistant.

Exam: BP 160/95. Fundoscopy shows retinal angiomas. Cranial nerves otherwise intact; strength, reflexes, sensation and coordination normal; gait steady.

Labs today: hemoglobin 13.2, hematocrit 39.8%, fasting glucose 88, calcium 9.6. Plasma free normetanephrine 568 pg/mL (ref <148), metanephrine 42 -- resulted 12/2.

MRI brain 11/26: left cerebellar hemangioblastoma with nodular enhancement, 1.4 cm (1.1 cm in 2022), no cyst or hydrocephalus.

Impression: Mild growth of the left cerebellar hemangioblastoma; no mass effect. Headaches/dizziness may relate, though no cerebellar signs on exam. Left eye symptoms more likely retinal -- ophthalmology already scheduled. Normetanephrine remains elevated; defer to PCP/endocrinology.
Plan: Observation; repeat MRI brain in 6 months. Neurosurgical opinion if further growth, cyst formation or progressive symptoms.

Neurology

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY -- RETINA, 12/10/2024

Returning (last seen 1/2023) with several weeks of blurred and partially lost vision in the left eye.

VA: 20/20 OD, 20/40 OS. IOP normal. Anterior segments quiet.
Dilated exam:
OD -- normal; no angioma; no diabetic retinopathy.
OS -- one of the previously treated temporal peripheral angiomas has enlarged, with a prominent feeder vessel; the second treated lesion is scarred and flat. Macula flat. No diabetic retinopathy.

Impression: Enlarging retinal angioma, left eye, VHL.
Procedure: laser photocoagulation to the enlarging lesion OS today, tolerated well.
Plan: recheck every 6-12 months. Call for any new vision change.

Retina Service
